payload.summary: Accept only the alkalinity budget-guard amendment. The other proposals either describe code that is not present in this review branch or point at a separate open backlog item rather than a correctness defect in the alkalinity patch itself.

votes.rationale: `update_molt_stress` does contain an unguarded `/ params.gh_min_d`, but with the enforced non-negative GH state the branch is unreachable when `gh_min_d == 0`, so this is not a concrete divide-by-zero defect. The cited `molt_mineral_modifier` helper is also not present in this branch, which makes the amendment a defensive consistency preference rather than a required fix.

This review branch's `molt_cycle` does not scale `failed_molt_accum` or recovery by `failed_stage_count` / `successful_stage_count`; it still applies a single fixed `+0.3` or `-0.35` adjustment per resolved molt day. The amendment describes a different implementation, so it does not identify a real issue in the code under review.

The cited geometry-scaling gaps are real separate backlog work under open bead `tanksim-6e5.5.6`, but they are unrelated to and untouched by the current `tanksim-6e5.4.7` alkalinity-accounting patch. As written, this amendment does not identify a correctness, safety, or robustness defect in the proposed alkalinity changes themselves.

This is a real robustness gap. The patch adds alkalinity to `BudgetDelta`, `BudgetTotals`, `Element`, and explicit water-change accounting, but `enforce_tracked_tick_budget_guard` still checks only nitrogen and carbon. That means a bad explicit alkalinity delta can pass `step_hours()` silently in normal execution and only be caught by optional external assertions, so the engine-level guard should be extended to alkalinity as well.
